newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: KLM sees lower 2nd half op income.
newsitem.headline: KLM sees lower 2nd half op income.

text.p: KLM Royal Dutch Airlines said on Tuesday it expected second half operating income to be lower than last year, due largely to higher fuel costs.

"We expect operating income to improve over last year, except for fuel costs which will be approximately 125 million guilders higher (than 106 million guilders in the first half year). On balance, operating income in the second half is expected to be lower than last year," it said in a statement.

"Taking into account the expected increase in fuel costs for the full year of 231 million guilders (150 million after tax), we expect net income after tax for 1996-97 to decrease approximately 150 million guilders compared to last year before any provision for costs of restructuring," it said in a statement.
